spirit: An Owing whose every line is true and still unjust: the player sees it stand and chooses what to pay for it.
premise: At the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, Never-Sold, born owing and long free, the one who remembers every bought-out name, sends you to an ex-Archein estate on the swamp road just north of the town. A woman there, grey from years away from her tree, has worked off a boat for eleven years. Never-Sold meets you at the estate's landing and makes her point to the steward in one exchange: every line of his book is true, and the Owing still stands. You can steal the estate's debt book from the work shed, by its lock, unseen, and use it to bring her buy-out down; or cut her loose at night, slipping her into the channel, where she cannot drown, while you keep the two estate men off her unseen, by blade or by bow. She lives either way.
changed: The estate moves from the Dres Rows (another worldspace) to an ex-Archein estate just north of Blackrose (gap-register QA3). The debt book is a thing the player steals (the ex-Archein families keep the ledgers, vibe §5, §9), not a prop read aloud. Each choice changes only a greeting later. Never-Sold has no escort: she meets the player at the estate landing.
why: The line's spirit is the true account that is still unjust; one exchange and one choice keep it.
lore: story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md §2-3; story/lore/topics/labour-and-bondage.md §1 (cannot drown); story/lore/extrapolation/gap-register.md §8 QA3; story/lore/blackrose.md

spirit: Fire in the cells of the Rose's outer post: whom the player brings out decides whose names survive.
premise: At the Chainbreakers' house in Blackrose, Never-Sold sends you to the Rose's outer post on the edge of town, from which the road runs a day's march to the prison itself: the cells under the post have caught fire, and how it started nobody says. Three the heirs hold are inside: a man held for speaking against them, a woman held for a killing, and the estate woman's mother, held on the heirs' own reckoning of her Owing. The heirs' gate-keepers will not go in. You go in through the smoke alone. Each cell is reached its own way: one by its lock, one by climbing a collapsed way, one by diving a flooded cell. When the first of them is out, the way burns shut behind you, and the gate-keepers say so plainly: only one comes out. Whoever lives speaks the names of the others, and those are carved on the heirs' stakes.
changed: The reading of burnt registers becomes a rescue from fire: people, not papers. The place is the outer post's cells; the Rose's lower levels, their sealed door and the old dead belong to BC04, and no heirs go in with the player. The Rose and the town are a day apart in the lore; the heirs keep an outer post at the town's edge, at BM&V's own 'Black Rose Jail' marker, and the prison proper lies a day's march beyond (gap-register QA4). White Rose and the Dres Rows leave this quest.
why: The line's burden (who counts as the Rose's) is carried by people in a fire.

spirit: A broker who freed hundreds and still hires them out: the player takes a side and pays for it.
premise: Ussa-Rekh works Soulrest's open dock among the crews. For thirty years he bought out Owings, and now he hires out the crews he freed; they say he saved them and they say he sold them. He gave each freed hand a carved token of the Owing he bought, and he keeps a crew's tokens in a chest in his cabin on the dock. That crew comes to him to end their last season early, and he refuses them. For the crew, you take their tokens from his cabin, by its lock, unseen, so they can break them before him; for him, you face the crew's boss in a brawl. Stand with the crew and he hires neither you nor them again; stand with him and the crew lose their trade on the dock.
changed: The broker sits on Soulrest's open dock, where the lore puts the indentured crews (labour §3), not Blackrose and not on a barge. The crew's claim is held in tokens, not papers. Each side's cost is a concrete loss, his hire or the crew's trade, and it changes only a greeting later.
why: Kept; the line's ambiguity of rescue and ownership.

spirit: The player is nobody on an Owing gang, processed at a work barge, and in the first hour sees a cell of the Unbound Root take the state's satchel, a Hist withdraw and a clutch die, and saves one witness.
premise: A new game opens in the hold of a debt-labour broker's barge moored at Lilmoth's dock, where an Owing gang hired to Hereguard Plantation is processed: the broker's overseer reads the roll aloud with the months added for food, and character creation is the processing itself: the player answers with a name, silence or an insult, and goes on. An An-Xileel courier walks with them upriver as cover, quiet about whom he serves: the one servant of the state among them. The overseer marches the gang along the shore to their camp at the edge of Hereguard's paddies (BlackMarsh -1,0), where the gang families keep a Hist cutting from Nine Bends with their clutch at its roots. Cuts-the-Old-Knot's cell strikes the courier at dusk, takes the satchel, looks at the player and leaves; the roll burns in the camp's fire, and the camp breaks into fire and shallow-water escape. The cell's harvest at the cutting's roots cuts the tree from its eggs; the cutting withdraws, and that night the clutch dies. The player saves one witness and gets away through the shallows.
changed: The barge and camp move from near Alten Corimont (not in BM&V) to Lilmoth's dock and the edge of Hereguard's paddies, where a new game lands. The gang is a local arrangement of a debt-labour broker and the plantation, not an arm of the state (owner Q7, quest-plan-deltas; prisons: no state work camp); the courier is the state's only presence. Hereguard has no Hist (hist-placement), so the camp keeps a cutting (gap-register QA1, an invention). It replaces Phase 1's lightest start. The hold cell's vanilla Skyrim location is cleared (we.mq01.hold-location). The collapse is staged in pockets of at most six active actors.
why: Every authored beat kept; only the place and the gang's master change, to fit BM&V and the lore.

spirit: Survivors piece together the attack under the Veiled Reed's eye, and Nesh-Deeka offers a dead prisoner a pardon on condition; the sap-dreams begin.
premise: At dawn, at the burnt camp at Hereguard, the player tastes the sap the cell spilled on the shed floor, among its jar-rings, and dives off the end of the burnt boards for the dead man's brass tag on the bottom, as the stranger on the shore directs. Two of the Veiled Reed's unmarked people take the hurt, the player among them, to an unmarked Lilmoth house a fish-trader keeps for them; the overseer has marched the unhurt back to the barge at Lilmoth's dock. Behind a screen Nesh-Deeka hears the night and sees that nobody can claim the player: she offers the Reed's protection, the house's door and a stipend on condition the player serves, and wants the survivor's account before the Reed's people see the survivor home. That night the first sap-dream comes: a ring of root ledges climbed to a door nobody built, and a voice.
changed: The guarded river station (Stormhold in the source) becomes an unmarked Lilmoth house kept through a Lilmoth intermediary (QA8), with no guards: Lilmoth denies the state, so the Reed works there deniably. The reading of the attack happens at the aftermath. The broker's bargain of the earlier rework is cut (owner 2026-11-06: law and custom only as background). The dream reuses the hold, emptied by MQ01's crew parent and its door locked, with fog and a ring of root ledges (placed statics, no tree) to climb.
why: Kept whole; the station is a house because Lilmoth has six rooms and denies the state.

spirit: A Hist community in trouble: the player recognises the dark uxith from the camp, and untangles disease, sabotage, grief and ritual.
premise: East of Lilmoth, the Hist of a stilt village on the leech water has turned its face: the tending-ground closed, the tenders grieving, the uxith dark, as at the camp. The village blames its leeches and its tree-minder. The player fights down through the leeches to a root cut and sealed with the village's own gum, learns from the tree-minder (watched by night) that he hid the cut, crosses the leech water on the gum trail and takes the jars of sap from the cell's camp by stealth or the blade. The player carries the jars and the tree-minder's knife back to the cut root, which clears the tree-minder.
changed: The Shadowfen Hist settlement becomes BM&V's unnamed Village east of Lilmoth (Low-Reed Village, QA6), whose leech water supplies the false cause and the danger. It is not the Hatching Pools. The earlier rework's hearing, award and weirs are cut (owner 2026-11-06).
why: BM&V's village has the people, the chief, the water and the leeches.

spirit: The Reed sends the player across the marsh to Helstrom, a safe city at the edge of a lethal basin, past the empty seat of the Scalded Throne, to tell its tree-minder and a Nisswo what a cut Hist looks like.
premise: With what the player found at Low-Reed Village, Nesh-Deeka sends them to Helstrom, where the interior's tree-minders and Nisswo gather and carry news home: the Reed cannot say it there, so the player will. The coast ship's door at Lilmoth's stop leads through the ship to its door on Helstrom's river landing; from there the way in is the marsh itself, root and shallows, with two giant wasps nesting at its far bend over a drowned root channel, to the levy's gate, where the warden says what the basin does. The hall of the Scalded Throne, a plain seat of root and reed that has stood empty for centuries and may never have been filled, is still swept, and the city sells in its outer room; the grove is behind the hall, where the tree-minder Kaska-Meen keeps her watch and Ei-Tuja, a travelling Nisswo, argues with her at the root's foot. The player tells one of them that a Hist that falls silent and a Hist whose root was cut are two things.
changed: The fast convoy from Alten Corimont becomes BM&V's ship (01Ship, cell 0AA665) entered by two doors: the door at Lilmoth's stop (0AA837, pair 0AA664, 7,-1) and the ship's door to the river landing (23D496, pair 0830A8, BlackMarsh2 -10,12, BM&V's own map marker 'Helstrom'), the landing door given by its place in the ship (measured at build). The Reed's two escorts, the ambush and the leave for Reed watchers are cut; the way in is the marsh, with two of BM&V's own giant wasps at its far bend at a fixed level (band 1). The gate is LQ30's BM&V gate (we.lq30.trail) and MQ05 owns no gate row. BM&V's two hall merchants stay in the outer room. The grove is a grove, not a tree; Kaska-Meen is a tree-minder of the interior who sits in Helstrom's assembly, and the dispute is colour at the grove's foot, in the evening.
why: Every §21 beat kept as a journey; BM&V provides the ship, the landing, Helstrom's people and the hall.

spirit: The Chapter's first test: get a stolen keepsake back from a thief without harm, by watching and talking, then go down to the Chapter.
premise: At Soulrest a Khajiit trader on the dock sends you to Deep-In-Her-Cups, who keeps the Chapter's desk in a back room and drinks nothing: the Chapter wants to see how you work. One thief took a keepsake, a necklace of polished blue jaspers, from another, and it must come back without harm. You watch the thief's round of the dock by day from cover; if he sees you watching, he moves the necklace. You learn whom he drinks with and where he sleeps on the boardwalk, and get it back by talk, trade or a quiet hand, not by breaking in. Caught, he runs rather than fights. Harm him and she pays nothing and says why, and sends you on all the same: by the coast ship from Soulrest to Lilmoth and the Chapter, whose way down is a trapdoor on Pusbottom's outskirts under Lilmoth.
changed: The tavern becomes Soulrest's one house (the fence's back room) and the boardwalk; the thief lives outdoors, so there is a round to watch, kept by his own packages. The desk is Deep-In-Her-Cups, the line's patron of restraint (36-cast-roster); a Khajiit trader is her front on the dock (Khajiit at Soulrest, vibe §8). The thief is cowardly, so he flees when caught, by his npc setting and no script. The trip to Lilmoth is by the coast ship that stops at Soulrest (we.name.soulrest). The Chapter is native and its seat is Pusbottom (guilds-and-orders); BM&V's dungeon under Lilmoth stands in for the room above a pawnshop, reached by BM&V's trapdoor two squares north of Pusbottom.
why: Kept; the first test is the line's restraint ethic.
lore: story/lore/topics/guilds-and-orders.md (the Night-Reed Chapter); story/lore/soulrest.md; story/lore/topics/material-culture.md (blue jaspers)

spirit: A dive for a lockbox three clients want, which proves all three lied.
premise: In the Chapter under Pusbottom, Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence, gives you the job. On Pusbottom's canal front in Lilmoth a merchant's stilt house has fallen from its stilts into the canal, and beside it on the canal floor lies a lockbox of pledged things: a carved token, a charm and a strand of Kothringi Glass Beads. Three clients each want it, and talk draws out each one's lie: one swears the token was carved for her clutch, one that the charm was only pledged and never sold, one that the beads are old family work. Ripper eels, slaughterfish at a fixed level, hunt the canal; you slip past them by stealth and timing, open the box's lock or bring it up whole, and swim out. Each thing in it gives the lie to one claim. You end it by handing the box to one client, or by selling a lie back to its teller.
changed: An ex-Archein estate's counting house becomes a merchant's stilt house fallen into the canal, holding pledges, not accounts (Lilmoth is a merchant city of sunken villas, lilmoth.md); the dive is the act. Bent-Spine (npc.mercantile-coast.lilmoth-divers-yard.night-reed-fence, an existing Chapter row) gives the job. The house is the fallen stilt house in the Pusbottom canal. The canal's ripper eels are canon (ecology-encounters-loot); eel-slime, their counter, waits for TG10. The box lies in the open beside the house, so the authored air pocket and escape are dropped: the player swims out. The shape is THEFT; no ending is carried forward.
why: Kept; the dive and the three liars are the quest.
